pages.text: Cold is a constant threat in frigid climates. When your body temperature drops below your comfortable range, you'll begin suffering from hypothermia, which can be just as deadly as hyperthermia if not properly managed.
pages.title: Freezing

pages.text: As you freeze, you'll experience severe effects:$(li)Slowness effect$(li)Mining Fatigue$(li)Damage$(li)with frost overlay

Several factors decrease your temperature:$(li)Low ambient temperature - tundra, mountains$(li)Wind chill - exposed areas$(li)Cold fluids - water, especially deep water$(li)Cold blocks - ice, snow$(li)Being wet - water conducts heat away$(li)Lack of sun - night, caves, shade$(li)High altitude - mountains are colder
pages.title: What Causes Cold

pages.text: $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wind)$(l)Wind$()$()$(br)Wind increases cooling. Find caves, build enclosed structures, or get behind walls to block the wind.$(br2)$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wetness)$(l)Stay Dry$()$()$(br)Wetness multiplies cold effects. Avoid water, rain, and snow. If you get wet, find shelter immediately and wait to dry.
pages.title: Staying Warm

pages.text: $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#radiant_source)$(l)Warm Blocks$()$()$(br)Position yourself near fires, lit forges, or other heat-emitting blocks. Even a small campfire can keep you alive.$(br2)$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#solar_radiation)$(l)Sun$()$()$(br)During the day, stay in open sunny areas. Solar radiation provides significant warmth, especially in low wind.

$(l:tfc:thermia/clothing)$(li)Insulation$()$(br)Wear wool or thick clothing. These can help slow the pull of the environment. THey can however also block heat from sources. Carry extra insulating items in your inventory for additional protection.$(br2)$(l)Time Your Activities$()$(br)Travel and work during midday when the sun is strongest. Shelter in place during night and storms.

Water is extremely dangerous in cold:$(li)Immersion rapidly drains body heat$(li)Wetness persists after leaving water$(li)Deep water increases cold exposure$(li)Freezing water can trap you$(br2)If you must cross water, do so quickly and dry off immediately by a fire.
pages.title: Water Dangers

pages.text: Humid cold is the worst. Just above freezing, wet and damp at the same time — your temperature plummets and drying takes forever. Don't get wet to begin with. In really cold biomes you'll need everything: good clothes, a fire, a roof, and sunshine. One of those alone won't cut it.
pages.title: Damp Cold

pages.text: Surviving cold winters requires preparation:$(l:tfc:thermia/interior)$(li)Build insulated shelters$()$(li)Stock firewood for continuous heat$(li)Wear full wool or leather gear$(li)Avoid unnecessary exposure$(li)Keep food and water accessible$(li)Never travel during snow
pages.title: Winter

pages.text: High altitudes present unique challenges:$(li)Temperatures drop with elevation$(li)Wind is stronger and more constant$(li)Less shelter available$(br2)Bring extra insulation, portable heat sources, and plan escape routes to lower elevations.
pages.title: Mountain Climbing
